newsitem.title: USA: NYC workfare leads to jobs for only 10 pct - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC workfare leads to jobs for only 10 pct - paper.

text.p: Less than 10 percent of the participants in New York City's workfare program, the largest in the nation, reported finding fulltime jobs, the New York Times said in its Monday edition.

But nearly two-thirds of the 122,700 peple who have been in the program, which began in early 1994, left it a few months later, though the city has no records of whether they succeeded in finding employment.

Their departure saved New York City $175 million in this year alone, but what they now are doing to support themselves is a bit of a mystery. City officials were quoted as saying that the majority who left the program probably found jobs, noting that the homelss rate has not climbed significantly during this period, while the crime rate has fallen.

Some of the private firms who have hired large groups of former workfare participants for real jobs said they were pleased with the program, but told the paper that only a few workers have kept their new jobs longer than a few months.

New York City's workfare program is drawing increased attention because the sweeping reforms in the federal welfare program call for one quarter of the adults who collect welfare to work within two years, and half of them within five years.
